title: Inference Financial Plane Consolidator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a "Financial Plane" consolidator service that takes low-level inference telemetry (per-token traces, model variant IDs, routing metadata, host-level GPU time) and produces reconciled cost + P50/P95 latency breakdowns per (route, model_version, customer_id). This ticket implements the core aggregation and normalization layer used by Console insights and the billing attribution pipelines.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Produce deterministic per-route cost attribution with <1% variance vs nightly reference ledger for synthetic workload.
- Latency slices: compute client->response p50/p95 and breakdown contribution by network, runtime, and queuing.
- Support multi-tenant safeguards: budget guards, zero-impact sampling mode, and per-tenant sampling configs.
- Output: time-bucketed (1m, 1h) rows to BigQuery topic and an audit log for every reconciliation run to S3.
- Backfill compatibility with previous ledger format for 90 days.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We normalize token cost using kernel-time-derived cost factors rather than flat per-token price to better reflect GPU mix and quantization. Pros: closer to infra spend; Cons: heavier coupling to runtime telemetry — mitigated by a staged rollout.
- We will do two parallel aggregation modes during rollout: a) streaming approximate aggregator (low-latency, probabilistic sketches) and b) batch reconciler (exact but higher latency). Streaming output is exposed to Console with a "confidence" score; billing will only use batch reconciler until 2% drift SLA met.
- Route attribution uses ordered-join on request_id, but we also accept best-effort joins using hashed session windows when spans are missing. This reduces drop rate but requires documented bias.

Dataflow and interfaces:
- Input sources: runtime-span-kafka (token-level spans), routing-events-kafka, tenant-metadata-service (HTTP cache).
- Core service: consolidator (Go), consumes kafka, maintains in-memory time-windowed state for continuous stitching, emits 1m/1h rollups to outbox topic.
- Schema: flat rows (timestamp, window, route_id, model_version, customer_id, tokens_generated, kernel_ms, host_gpu_ms, inferred_cost_usd, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, confidence_tag, reconciled_by="batch|stream").
- Audit: store per-window raw reconciliation diffs to s3://redwood-inference-audits/finance/; link in Console UI for support teams.

Rollout plan:
1) Unit tests + local harness with synthetic traces.
2) Canary in staging reading staging topics, validate against staging reference ledger.
3) Deployment to canary cluster in prod writing to a new topic (console.cost.reconciler.v1.preview).
4) Compare streaming vs batch reconciler for 7 days, monitor drift.
5) Promote streaming to Console UI with confidence band only.
6) After drift <2% for 14 days, enable batch ledger as authoritative for billing.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Pipeline lag <30s for streaming output 95% of time.
- Reconciliation drift <2% compared to nightly exact-run.
- Reconciler error rate <0.1% and tombstone count per window <0.01%.
- Alerts: high drift, kafka consumer backlog, schema mismatch errors.

Migration notes:
- Backfill strategy: run batch reconciler against last 90 days using airflow job that replays raw topics into reconciler in an archived mode.
- Consumers (Console + billing) must accept new schema; backwards compatibility shim will emit older field names for 60 days.

PRs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COST/Financial+Plane+Consolidator (internal)
- Local test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-consolidator/tree/feature/ENG-901277-harness
- Spike PR (streaming aggregator): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-consolidator/pull/482
- Draft BigQuery schema: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1F_inferred_schema (view-only)

Recent updates / comments:
- 2025-11-10 | Aisha Patel: Initial spec posted; flagged dependency on runtime span change (ENG-31245).
- 2025-11-14 | Marco Li: Completed prototype of time-window stitcher. Found 12% undercount when spans missing end timestamps; added heuristic to estimate end using token rate.
- 2025-11-20 | SRE (Lara Gomez): Asked for backpressure behavior doc — added circuit-breaker with configurable queue limits per-tenant.
- 2025-11-26 | PM (Ravi Desai): Requested per-customer sampling control exposed via Tenant API — added dependency on tenant-metadata-service and new label "sampling_control".
- 2025-11-30 | Marco Li: Canary deployed to prod-readonly topic. Early validation shows streaming/batch drift = 4.1% for one noisy customer; opened follow-up ENG-901378 to investigate model-variant tagging gaps.
- 2025-12-02 | Aisha Patel: Decided to delay authoritative billing switch until ENG-901378 addressed. Running extra reconciliation for the noisy customer and adding tighter model_version canonicalization step in consolidator.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we include a per-token GPU-power estimate or rely purely on kernel_ms? (SRE prefers kernel_ms only for safety.)
- Final schema change window: how long to support v0 naming? Proposed 60 days but finance requested 90 days.

Acceptance test checklist (to mark Done):
- [ ] End-to-end test comparing consolidator vs reference for 30 synthetic tenants.
- [ ] Load test at 2x expected peak ingest for 72 hours with no data loss.
- [ ] Canary validation report with drift <2% for all customers except known exceptions tracked in ENG-901378.
- [ ] Runbook and rollback playbook published in Confluence and linked in Console.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the canonicalization logic (model_version mapping) and the trade-off between latency of streaming vs accuracy of batch. See spike PR for the streaming algorithm and the reconciler PR for exact join logic.
